segments.narration: Every wild tree of this species is genetically identical. The Wollemi pine, in sandstone gorges a hundred and fifty kilometres from Sydney.
segments.visual_query: wollemi sandstone gorge new south wales

segments.narration: September 1994. David Noble and two friends roped into an unexplored canyon and found trees with bubbly bark and ferny leaves. Nobody recognised them.
Botanists matched their pollen to fossil pollen from drill cores across the southern continents, stretching back ninety million years. So why only sixty trees?
Genetics answered it. A bottleneck within the last twenty-six thousand years cut them to perhaps one or two individuals. Every living tree descends from those.
The exact site stays secret. When the 2019 bushfires closed in, specialist crews flew in, laid irrigation lines and dropped retardant. The grove held.

verdicts.claim: The Wollemi pine was found on about 10 September 1994 by David Noble with two companions exploring canyons in Wollemi National Park, about 150 km north-west of Sydney.
verdicts.note: 93% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 3 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The tree's pollen matches fossil pollen named Dilwynites, recorded across the southern continents from roughly 90 million years ago, and fewer than 60 adult wild trees are known across four locations.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia gives fewer than 60 adults in four locations and names Dilwynites (Late Cretaceous to Pliocene). Britannica states Dilwynites pollen is common in Australian, New Zealand, Tasmanian and Antarctic fossil records dating back more than 90 million years, and the 2023 genome paper gives a Wollemia record of about 90 to 2.5 million years. IMPORTANT CAVEAT, which is why the narration claims only a pollen match and not an unchanged lineage: a 2002 review notes some Dilwynites records may belong to the sister genus Agathis, and Wikipedia states there are no unambiguous Wollemia macrofossils, so the popular 'extinct for 90 million years' framing is not supportable and is deliberately not used.

verdicts.claim: The genetic uniformity is consistent with a bottleneck 10,000 to 26,000 years ago that may have cut the population to one or two individuals.
verdicts.note: 79% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 2 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The grove's exact location is undisclosed, and during the 2019-2020 bushfire season specialist crews installed irrigation and dropped retardant to save it.
